entry.what_was_wrong: Two things on GET /api/gspc. (1) measured_on.model said the behavioural axis were measured on a '19-model fleet (8 tuned council specialists + 6 base models + frontier cross-lab models)', and measured_on.endpoint listed 'OpenRouter (cross-lab models)'. The published per-item rows those axis are graded on (csoai/gspc-peritem-rows-2026-08-12, revision 294e4cf9e8b72a00aa50de024b3ed3e7ab0b3361, peritem_sha256 0d8dacfbe7384a5d2f6a83e7455482ab75f935366bbb6e18da61cfdac8890dec, 13 files, 15,580 rows) hold 19 model ids: 6 base models and 13 of our own fine-tunes, and no other model. The count of our own models was wrong (8, not 13) and the text named a frontier cross-lab fleet that is not in the rows. Our own fine-tunes were already excluded before ranking; no public leader or determination rested on them. (2) The board published TIE on 8 model-comparison axis without saying how large a difference its test could have detected. On safety, continuity and conformance (36, 33 and 35 paired items; 6, 6 and 4 discordant) no difference up to the observed discordance reaches 80% power with the board's exact McNemar test at p<0.05, so a TIE there cannot be read as 'no difference between models'. The TIE determinations themselves are correct under the fixed 2026-08-13 rule.
entry.how_caught: A read-only diff (scripts/gspc_board_honesty_diff.py) lined up, per model-comparison axis, the board's separation state, the verdict in the rows' own SEPARATION_RESULT.json (own models excluded), the distinct items in the rows and the minimum detectable effect of the test, and counted the fleet from the model ids in the rows. It found 7 axis where board and rows agree, 6 where the board states UNTESTED with a published reason code, 1 (jail) whose determination comes from another source, and none that disagree. It flagged the fleet text and the endpoint text, and found that no axis carried distinct_items or an MDE.
entry.what_changed: measured_on.model is now derived at serve time from the model ids in the published rows (functions/api/_gspc_rows_power.ts, generated by scripts/gspc_separation_from_rows.py --power from the hash-bound rows). It states a 19-model fleet: 6 base models, ranked, and 13 CSOAI own fine-tunes, excluded before ranking and never counted in a comparison; no other model is in the rows. The 'OpenRouter (cross-lab models)' clause is removed from measured_on.endpoint. Every model-comparison axis now carries distinct_items (with its source) and mde: the smallest accuracy difference between the leader and the best base model that the board's own exact two-sided McNemar test (p<0.05) detects with 80% probability, given the axis's paired items and observed discordance rate, computed by exact binomial enumeration. Read on 2026-09-28: care 0.109 (199 items), governance 0.138 (237), affect 0.203 (41), provenance 0.288 (32), cross-reality 0.288 (32), machinery-conformity 0.306 (33), openness 0.329 (32); NOT_REACHABLE on safety, continuity, conformance, detector-interop and art5-safeguard; UNMEASURED on jail and swarm, whose served banks have no published paired rows (swarm's only published rows are its retired 3-item bank, where the MDE is NOT_REACHABLE). No separation determination changed: the board still reads 0 SEPARATED, 8 TIE, 6 UNTESTED. No signed bytes changed: the signed rows record (/interop/gspc-peritem-rows-2026-08-12.json, sha256 f64353e0…), the signed card index and the signed board snapshots are untouched; the producer now refuses to rewrite a record whose .signed.json binds other bytes. A new public state for a TIE the test could not resolve (UNDERPOWERED) is built but switched off pending the owner's ruling.
